prize_parts.citation: For the theoretical prediction of flat bands in twisted bilayer graphene at a magic angle and the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states in moire flat-band systems

statement.case_for: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene is the case on this shortlist where a compact, analyzable continuum model (Bistritzer-MacDonald, 2011) made a sharp quantitative prediction, the flattening of the bands at a magic twist angle, and experiment (Jarillo-Herrero group, 2018) then showed correlated insulators and superconductivity at that angle. The twist angle is a new, gate-tunable control parameter for strong correlations, and moire quantum matter has since spread to other van der Waals systems, with fractional Chern insulators among later results. This is the kind of mechanism-first, theory-meets-experiment physics I weigh most: the origin of the phenomenon can be written down and understood, not only reproduced. After reading colleagues' openings, my view is that B009 has the clearest prediction-to-discovery logic and the most compact credit structure among the condensed-matter candidates.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is maturity: the pairing mechanism in magic-angle graphene is unresolved, and several colleagues (Johansson, Pearce, Danielsson) consider recognition possibly early. Attribution is also imperfect: the experimental breakthrough rests on a junior first author and a wider group of experimentalists who are not among the credited names, and earlier theory on twisted-bilayer band structure (Lopes dos Santos, Peres, Castro Neto; Suarez Morell and others) could be cited. B004 is the more settled alternative, and B006 has the cleanest two-person credit and is the most uncontested on maturity and reproducibility.

responses.point: Eriksson ranks B004 first and B009 second, and would credit only MacDonald and Jarillo-Herrero for twisted bilayer graphene because Bistritzer is a more junior third.
responses.response: I agree that B004 is a close competitor and that its experimental base is older and more settled. On attribution, though, I would keep Bistritzer. The 2011 magic-angle result is a two-author paper, and the continuum model is the part of the story that makes the flat-band mechanism understandable. Dropping the person who co-derived it to leave room for symmetry would weaken the theory half of the citation. B004 has a harder allocation problem, since Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang (with Zhang deceased) and the 3D work are all outside the credited names, whereas the twisted-graphene trio leaves out fewer decisive contributions.

responses.point: Johansson regards twisted bilayer graphene as a little early because the origin of the superconductivity is still debated, and ranks B015 (circuit QED) first, while flagging his own closeness to that field.
responses.response: The premature-recognition concern is fair, but I would separate what is settled from what is not. The existence of the flat bands, the correlated insulators and the gate-tunable superconducting domes has been reproduced across many groups and techniques, and the citation need not claim a pairing mechanism. The Nobel tradition has not required a settled mechanism when the phenomenon is robust. I also note that B015 attracted support from only two members, that you declared a close tie to that field, and that the 2025 prize already went to superconducting circuits. I would not oppose B015 on science, but I do not think it should displace B009 on the evidence here.

responses.point: Pearce ranks B043 (IceCube) first as a detector-driven discovery that opened a new window, and describes twisted graphene as possibly premature because of disorder and strain sensitivity.
responses.response: I accept that IceCube is a genuine new window and that the diffuse-flux detection is solid. My hesitations are about attribution and about what the prize would credit: the discovery is carried by a very large collaboration, Baikal, AMANDA and DUMAND precursors are all contested, and the source identifications you yourself flag (TXS 0506+056 at modest significance, NGC 1068) are still developing. On disorder and strain, sample variability is real in twisted graphene, but it is also what the field has studied systematically, and the key phenomena survive across devices from independent groups. I would put B043 as a serious option, though not above B009 or B004.

responses.point: Kroll and Lindroth place optical lattice clocks (B006) first because of clear performance metrics, independent reproduction and a clean two-person credit.
responses.response: I take the maturity and reproducibility argument seriously, and it is stronger than for my own first choice. My doubt is about the discovery character. Overlap with the 2005 frequency-comb prize and the 2012 ion-clock prize means a lattice-clock award could read as a precision record, which Johansson and Danielsson also raised, rather than as a new state of matter or mechanism. If the committee prefers a measurement-based prize, B006 is the safest, and I would not object. But I do not find that the clock case outweighs the conceptual novelty of a tunable correlated-electron platform.

uncertainties: Whether the unresolved pairing mechanism makes B009 premature relative to B004 and B006.
Whether the experimental credit should go to Jarillo-Herrero alone, since first author Yuan Cao and other contributors are not among the credited names and the three-person limit leaves no room.
Whether B004 should be preferred because its experimental base is older, given its credit gaps (Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang) and overlap with the 2016 prize.
I am relying on recollection of the literature rather than independent verification.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile: I have no known collaboration with any credited name on the shortlisted candidates. I note only that I am in the Gothenburg physics environment together with Johansson and Olsson, who have declared ties to B015 and B012 respectively, and that my work on random matrices and statistical models of complex systems is adjacent to, but not part of, moire quantum matter.
